header: Rows that open on click, with no script at all
lead: Native disclosure markup: the browser owns the open state, the keyboard and the accessible name. Use it where the detail would swamp the page but a knowledgeable minority still wants it.

entries.title: Why details and summary rather than a script
entries.bodytext: Because everything an accordion needs already exists in HTML: a toggle, a labelled region, Enter and Space, and a state the browser can restore when a reader navigates back. Rebuilding that in JavaScript adds a dependency and a way for the band to break.

entries.title: Several rows can be open at once
entries.bodytext: None of the rows are grouped by a shared name, so opening one leaves the others alone. Where only one entry should ever be open, the capability tabs band is the right one instead.

entries.title: It prints open
entries.bodytext: A closed row would otherwise print as a headline with nothing underneath it. One print rule releases the disclosure's own box, which is the single thing the platform does not do on its own.
